scope: Pinned P_PCIE_INIT/pcie_init T8103 path only, including transitive PMGR/tunables and HV lifecycle. Current root survey trial remains read-only and has NO pcie_init. This receipt adds no host code or execution approval.
verdict: P_PCIE_INIT is a broad, state-changing controller initializer, not a bounded port0 survey prerequisite. No existing port-selective or power/clock-only PCIe API exists. Saved J293 ADT selects only bridge0, but shared PHY and PMGR writes exceed that port. Resolve shared ANS ownership, unsafe alias bookkeeping, HV ordering, live isolation and failure containment before proposing a separate initialization candidate.

provenance.license: Upstream source retains SPDX MIT; no upstream code copied or relicensed.

reference_adt.note: Private saved bytes, not new device observations. Guest removes the active USB0 apciec0 subtree; P_PCIE_INIT does not target apciec0/1 in either tree. No ADT payload, serial or firmware bytes reproduced.

api_and_scope.dispatch: src/proxy.h:164; src/proxy.c:618-622; proxyclient/m1n1/proxy.py:1212-1215: no-argument P_PCIE_INIT calls pcie_init, separate P_PCIE_SHUTDOWN calls pcie_shutdown.
api_and_scope.public_api: src/pcie.h:6-7 exposes only init(void)/shutdown(void); controller initializer is static (pcie.c:364). No port mask, port0 function, read-only mode or clock-only stop point.
api_and_scope.generic_non_t8140_scope: pcie.c:1080-1083 attempts /arm-io/apcie, /arm-io/apcie0 (same APCIE state), /arm-io/apcie-ge0 and /arm-io/apcie-ge1. Bitwise success aggregation executes all calls and returns success if any controller succeeds.
api_and_scope.ports: pcie.c:738-759 loops every #ports index and skips only absent bridge nodes. Saved J293 has #ports=3 but only pci-bridge0; ports1/2 core APPCLK/PERST/config loop is skipped. Neither alias nor GE node is present.
api_and_scope.shared_phy: Saved apcie-phy-tunables writes shared PHY+0x8 and +0x4004,+0x8004,+0xc004, including the ADT port0/1/2 PHY banks. AUSPMA tunables also cover all three port PHY-IP banks (shared base offsets through 0x1d024). Therefore even this one-bridge tree is not a port0-only hardware mutation.
api_and_scope.endpoint_scope: Bridge0 ADT contains both WLAN and Bluetooth functions. No function-selection/exclusion API or endpoint ownership guard; a port reset/link operation is shared. No USB-C apciec controller initialization is selected.

power_and_reset.selector: pmgr.c:340-356 reads clock-gates (not power-gates); both properties are [77,97,29] in this ADT.
power_and_reset.mutation: pcie.c:552 -> pmgr.c:459-462,420-436,255-291,95-114: recursively force each nonvirtual parent active (target 0xf); RMW clears AUTO_ENABLE bit28, WAS_CLKGATED bit9, WAS_PWRGATED bit8 and target bits3:0, then writes target0xf and polls actual bits7:4. No skip if already active and no saved-mode rollback. Successful path visits [32,77,32,77,97,29]. Other status/reset bits are preserved, not preflight-refused.
power_and_reset.shared_storage_dependency: Saved /arm-io/ans clock-gates=[103 APCIE_ST]; its parent closure is {103 APCIE_ST,98 ANS2,77 APCIE,32 IMX}. Init does not request 98/103, but rewrites their shared APCIE/IMX ancestors. No storage-isolation guarantee follows from absence of nvme calls.
power_and_reset.pmgr_reset: No pmgr_reset/pmgr_adt_reset call. The explicit RESET/DEV_DISABLE toggle implementation at pmgr.c:561-588 is not reached. PMGR parents are not intentionally powered down or reset by this T8103 path; changing shared modes remains a real mutation.
power_and_reset.phy_reset: pcie.c:618-651 requests common CLK0/1, waits ACKs, clears shared PHY reset bit7, sets RC PHYIF_RUN. Not an idempotent read/verify; changes shared PHY state.
power_and_reset.perst: pcie.c:902-913 sets port0+0x814 bit0 to deassert PERSTN, then polls RUN. It does not first assert PERST on T8103. It does not execute ADT function-perst/function-clkreq GPIO functions or use t-refclk-to-perst/perst-to-config delay properties. Those real saved properties remain outside its contract.
power_and_reset.power_rail: No GPIO/SMC/RTKit endpoint-power operation is called. Wi-Fi/BT rail power and external reset state are not established by a zero return.

t8103_write_sequence.action: Recursive PMGR active requests described above.
AXI tunables; write RC+0x4=0 (source labels semantics ???); common RC and shared PHY tunables.
Common PHY CLK0/1 requests and ACK polls; reset release; RC PHYIF RUN.
Read 11 calibration bitfields from fuse aperture 0x23d2bc000 and RMW their PHY-IP targets; then PLL and AUSPMA tunables. No fuse programming.
For each present bridge: port tunables, APPCLK enable, PERST deassert, RUN and not-BUSY polls. On this ADT only bridge0.

Enable root DBI read-only-register writes at ECAM+0x8bc, apply three root configuration/shadow tunable groups, set Gen2 maximum speed and one-lane width for this ADT, request speed change, clear DBI write-enable.
Read LINKSTS and mark port active without requiring LINK_UP; set controller initialized, dirty=false.

saved_tunables_audit.bounds_limit: This offline audit applies to the exact saved ADT only. tunables_apply_local_addr (tunables.c:101-130) validates record stride/size but not offset alignment/span/overflow before MMIO, and permits prior writes before a later failure. T8103 does not call the T8140-only up-front local-tunable preflight (pcie.c:543-547). A future candidate must bind/check the actual proxy ADT, not only the guest tree.
saved_tunables_audit.semantics_limit: No raw mask/value table exported. Bounded addresses do not establish every opaque RC/AXI/PHY tuning bit effect; RC+4 and some initialization operations are explicitly undocumented in the pinned source.

operation_matrix.operation: DART/IOMMU roots, TLB invalidate, translate/bypass modes
operation_matrix.source_result: No DART/IOMMU calls or direct DART register writes. All 191 saved tunables plus fixed T8103 writes avoid dart-apcie0 aperture. Does not consume dart-tunables-instance-0.
operation_matrix.limit: Does not establish current lock, bypass, enabled stream, root ownership, RID mapping or DMA containment. No automatic bypass is acceptable.

operation_matrix.source_result: Explicit MSI map programming is guarded for other SoCs (pcie.c:814-857,1021-1029), not T8103. Saved port0 tunables only touch +0x140,+0x144,+0x800; no port MSI configuration/address/base or RID2SID-table writes. No endpoint MSI enable or handler allocation.
operation_matrix.limit: Existing MSI/RID state remains inherited and unvalidated; cannot claim interrupts disabled or a working MSI path.

operation_matrix.source_result: No DMA buffer/ring/descriptor setup, transaction submission, endpoint BAR programming, PCI command bus-master-enable write or downstream device scan in this routine. ECAM writes are root-port configuration.
operation_matrix.limit: Shared clocks/reset release/link enable can wake endpoints with inherited state. No bus-master-off or quiescence proof, no isolation installation; absence of software DMA submission is not proof no autonomous DMA can occur.

operation_matrix.source_result: No firmware upload, firmware command queue, flash write or fuse programming. Reads calibration fuses and applies ADT hardware tunables.
operation_matrix.limit: Endpoint firmware state and tune-bit side effects are not observed.

operation_matrix.source_result: No nvme_init/read/flush or block/filesystem/NVRAM/boot-policy call. P_NVME_* are separate proxy cases (proxy.c:625-636); nvme_init selects /arm-io/ans (nvme.c:373).
operation_matrix.limit: Shared APCIE/IMX PMGR ancestry with ANS means no claim of zero storage-controller side effects. Persistent-state integrity must remain a separate recovery/ownership gate.

concrete_lifecycle_blockers.finding: APCIE alias probe erases successful state on this exact ADT.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.evidence: pcie.c:377-384 clears initialized/active_ports before checking path. After /arm-io/apcie succeeds and clears dirty, pcie.c:1081 calls absent /arm-io/apcie0 with the same APCIE state. That call clears initialized/active_ports and returns -1; success from the first call survives and global pcie_initialized becomes true.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.consequence: A zero proxy result can coexist with forgotten active hardware; shutdown skips the controller at1104. Future lifecycle must fix/model this rather than rely on the bug.

concrete_lifecycle_blockers.evidence: proxyclient/m1n1/hv/__init__.py:1383 calls p.hv_init; src/hv/hv.c:170 calls pcie_shutdown unconditionally and ignores its return.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.consequence: Calling init before HV.init is not a stable contract. With correct bookkeeping HV.init asserts port PERST/clears APPCLK and PHY requests; with this ADT alias bug it instead silently skips them. Neither behavior is an acceptable implicit ordering dependency.

concrete_lifecycle_blockers.finding: Failure is partial and shutdown is not rollback.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.evidence: dirty set at549 before power, many later return -1 paths; dirty retry refused373-375. shutdown1098-1105 returns when global false or controller not initialized.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.consequence: A failed first init leaves writes in place without cleanup. A failure while DBI write-enable is set can leave it enabled. Successful shutdown also leaves PMGR modes, tunables and fuse-calibration writes unrestored. Do not treat pcie_shutdown or a second init as a recovery transaction.

concrete_lifecycle_blockers.finding: No complete live ownership or isolation preflight.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.evidence: T8103 path checks compatible/reg geometry but not current ANS/shared-clock ownership, inherited endpoint activity, DART isolation, GPIO rail/reset state or all tunables before first write.
concrete_lifecycle_blockers.consequence: The source is insufficient to authorize simply inserting this proxy call before the read-only survey.

timing_and_success_limits.bounded_polls: poll32 utils.h:454-463 is a decrement loop with 1us delay per unsuccessful completed read, not a wall-clock deadline. PMGR:10000 iterations per active request; CLK0/1:50000 each; port RUN/not-BUSY:250000 each. On this saved successful one-port topology six PMGR requests plus four PHY/port polls imply about 660ms of maximum explicit polling delays plus read/write/log overhead; this is NOT a hardware or host timeout guarantee.
timing_and_success_limits.mmio_fault: A stalled/aborting MMIO access is not contained by the poll loop. There is no transaction-wide timeout or automatic rollback.
timing_and_success_limits.success: Return0 only means at least one controller reached the end (or global initialized shortcut); no LINK_UP assertion, endpoint identity, DART readiness, DMA safety or functional Wi-Fi/NVMe result. Never substitute it for the actual survey snapshot.
timing_and_success_limits.survey: Existing survey guards stay strict: power target+actual, no RESET/AUTO/disable, PHY requests+ACKs/no reset, RC_RUN, APPCLK/PERST/RUN before every DART read. No source or guard changes made.

ordered_residual_gate: Use the current unmodified read-only survey result first. If NOT_READY, preserve its numeric prerequisite snapshot; do not auto-call PCIe init or weaken the guard.

For a later separate candidate, bind the actual proxy ADT and exact m1n1 bytes; enumerate every required shared power/clock/tunable write and prove shared ANS, USB/recovery and endpoint ownership. Investigate the minimal power/clock dependency without assuming full endpoint reset/link enable is necessary. No existing port0-only API provides this.

Resolve P1 alias-state and P2 HV-ordering explicitly in reviewed source/contract with source-linked fake tests; require correct no-op, partial-failure, absent-alias and shutdown cases. No host insertion is approved by this review.

Establish a genuine fail-closed endpoint quiescence/isolation plan before releasing reset or link. Preserve DART ownership, prohibit bypass/root adoption, firmware and DMA setup; no partial-state retry or shared-domain powerdown as cleanup.

Only then assemble a separately reviewed, explicitly opt-in mutation candidate with one bounded attempt, durable intent/actual-write observations, exact proof limits and the existing independently controlled Linux recovery. Root owns any authorization, build and hardware work.
